content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper studies Data-Free Class Incremental Learning which aims to sequentially learn tasks with access only to data from the current one. This work focuses on the saliency drift problem which is associated with catastrophic forgetting and proposes  RObust Saliency Supervision consisting of three designs:(1)a teacher-student architecture leveraging low-level l tasks to supervise the model with global saliency; (2) boundary-guided mid-level saliency drift regularization;(3) saliency noise injection. Experimental results show that the network is able to reduce saliency drift along the incremental learning stages and state-of-the-art performance is achieved.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
(1) It is interesting to improve the robustness of DFCIL via saliency supervision.
(2) A novel framework is proposed to reduce saliency drift in incremental learning and the visual comparison with existing methods show the effectiveness.
(3) Ablation experiments on each module are provided.

Weaknesses:
(1) The paper is basically well-written while some writing issues.
In Section 2.2, the paper says "The boundary map is computed with a Laplacian filter over the estimated saliency map". So I guess that T_b(x)=Laplace(T(x)). But in the paper, the formulation of T_b(x) is not introduced. And Equation 3 makes me confused because Laplace(T_b(x)) is used.

Some grammatical errors exist, e.g., "We show that ROSS can be easily integrated into other state-of-the-art methods".

(2) Visualization questions. It is weird that the input images of Task1-5 are different in Figure 6 and the author should explain their difference. Besides, There is obvious saliency drift of Task5-Stage 4 compared to Task1-Stage 4 and Task3-Stage 4. So I doubt whether the network could recover saliency drift as claimed.

(3) Ablation study. From the last two rows in Table 3, it seems that the improvement brought by DBS is minor.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: This paper provides several novel plug-in modules for Data-Free Class Incremental Learning. The experimental results show superior performance over baselines. But some technical details are not clearly introduced. The ablation study and some visualization do not support the proposed modules' claimed strength.
content.summary_of_the_review: The proposed method is reasonable and experimental results show the performance. But some issues with writing, visualization, and ablation are mentioned above.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper focuses on the saliency drift problem of the Data-Free continual saliency detection task. The authors propose a teacher-student framework that the teacher module predicts the saliency map and provides a dilated boundary as the student module supervision. Extra noises are introduced to enhance the representative ability of the detection module. As a plug-and-play module, combining it with other methods can improve the detection result quantitatively.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Pros:
	Teacher-student design can provide strong guidance in learning how to detect saliency objects. Also, teacher networks generate the saliency prediction and the object boundary as the side information to guide the encoder part. Although the setting is not that novel, the student module can learn most of the information from the teacher's guidance.
	The side information from the object boundary forces the encoder to learn both object and boundary representation so that the encoder will not only learn how to detect the object but also the boundary of the object.
	The noise project module ensures the encoder will not bias by the non-saliency pixels and the background.
	Experimental result shows the improvement in the accuracy of other methods with the proposed module.
Cons/Question:
	As the teacher network is pretrained and strong, it can provide relatively good supervision. However, the ground truth is better than the teacher network. Also, the ground truth can generate boundary information too. So, why not use the ground truth to generate boundary information to guide the training of the encoder?
	Is the classifier predicting the semantic label of the input? If yes, the model will have extra guidance in training the network. Or if not, what is the guidance of the classifier?
	The title ‘RETHINKING SALIENCY IN DATA-FREE CLASS INCREMENTAL LEARNING’ discusses data-free class incremental learning. But in the paper, there are almost no discussions about the incremental learning part. How can the proposed model solve or alleviate the catastrophic forgetting problem? The enhancement of the encoder can partially improve the problem. Is there any special design for solving the problem?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The idea of using side information in solving the prediction drift problem is novel. While the teacher-student framework and extra guidance are not that novels.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper proposed a solution of solving the prediction drift problem in Data-free class incremental learning. The method is simple and effective. While some of the problem in incremental learning was not discussed. In its current state, the paper is not ready for publication.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This work studies a new subtype of continual learning, that is, Data-Free Class Incremental Learning (DFCIL). The authors argue that privacy concerns and restrictions on the long-term storage of data make DFCIL be of great interest. Also, similar to other continual learning settings, alleviating catastrophic forgetting is an important goal in the proposed learning paradigm. The authors propose a new framework, RObust Saliency Supervision (ROSS), for mitigating the negative effect of saliency drift. The proposed framework is evaluated on CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet, and ImageNet-Subset.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths

1. This work studies a new subtype of continual learning. The DFCIL may be practically useful in some scenarios.

2. The experiments provide a comparison with relevant and state-of-the-art continual learning methods.

Weaknesses

1. The connection between the DFCIL paradigm and the Non-Exemplar Class-Incremental Learning (NECIL, Zhu et al., 2022) paradigm is unclear. In my understanding, DFCIL is an extension of NECIL, but the connection should be explicitly discussed for clarity.

2. The authors attempt to justify that the privacy concerns and restrictions on the long-term storage of data are two reasons why DFCIL is worth being studied. However, I am not convinced. Why not study differential privacy in continual learning? Why are there restrictions on the long-term storage of data when we know the storage has been developed to be cost-effective nowadays?

3. It is a bit abrupt to introduce that saliency drift is a priority and a key factor to DFCIL. Three qualitative examples in Figure 1 do not show clear implications. In my view, saliency drift is more like an effect of catastrophic forgetting, rather than a cause.

4. The proposed method relies on the teacher model T, i.e., CSNet (Cheng et al., 2021), according to Equations (2), (3), and (4). T could also introduce false predictions that lead to defective student models. Why is CSNet the only choice for T?

5. The experimental protocol is not convincing. In Section 3.1, the classes are split to $F + C \times T$, which means the first task contains F classes, and the next T tasks each contain C classes. However, why separating the classes like that is not clear. Moreover, how to determine F, i.e., the critical point, may lead to different conclusions. However, we do not see the analysis of this point.

6. The experimental results may not be extensive. SSRE (Zhu et al., 2022) provides the results on CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet on the metrics accuracy and forgetting, but the proposed method is only evaluated on CIFAR-100 on the metrics accuracy and forgetting.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity: The paper is easy to follow, but the points in the paper may not be well connected as discussed in the weaknesses.

Quality: I think it is at the average level.

Novelty: The problem is novel, but the methodology is not much specific to tackle the problem.

Reproducibility: As shown in Figure 2, the proposed framework involves a number of components. Without providing the code, the experimental results may not be easily reproduced.
content.summary_of_the_review: As discussed in the strengths and weaknesses, I acknowledge that this work studies a novel problem, but there is room to improve the quality of the paper. Therefore, I am neutral with the paper at this point.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a Robust Saliency Supervision (ROSS) framework for data-free class incremental learning. It uses a teacher-student approach, where teacher network provide supervision of salient regions and boundaries for student network.  Dilated boundary maps and saliency noises are applied to avoid saliency drift. Experiments on CIFAR-100 are conducted.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
1. The technical details are clearly presented. Experiments have justifed the effectiveness of the proposed methodl

2. The overall contribution is not significant. The teacher-student idea is not new and the proposed dilated boundary maps and saliency noises injection to prevent saliency drift seems heuristic. The insight brought by the proposed method is limited.

3. No related works are discussed. It is not clear how the proposed method different from previous works.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is overall clear presented. However, the novelty and contribution is limited. It may be hard to obtain important new knowledge from the proposed method. The idea of using teacher-student network for increamental learning with saliency supervision has been explored. The proposed techniques like dilated boundary maps and noises injection is somewhat trivial. It is also unkown whether the proposed method can be also applicable to other incremental tasks (like detection or segmentation) besides image classification.
content.summary_of_the_review: My major concern of this paper is the limited contribution and novelty which I believe fails to meet the bar of ICLR.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
